headlineNote: Previous issue (2026-10-03) used a question. Attribute any claim to its source (e.g. Mistral says / preprint says); do not state company figures as fact.
closing: Optional thread links research and invention only (AI holding a person's own life: accuracy and user control). Keep research and invention adjacent. Do not extend to news.

news.why: Hype-heavy launch (reported 1T parameters, beats-rivals claims) where company claims need separating from independent evidence. Recent 09-30 and 10-03 issues both used this for news, but the combination with the other two formats is new.

research.why: Contested, easy-to-misread preprint with candid limitations (10 users, ethics oversight, re-identification). Reader questions fit better than an explainer, which was used last issue; by-the-numbers was used 09-30.

invention.why: Local photo/video search app vs cloud photo search and built-in OS search lets the honest caveats (Mac-only, indexing cost) sit in a table. Combination qa + claim-vs-evidence + comparison does not match 09-30 (by-the-numbers/claim-vs-evidence/comparison) or 10-03 (explainer/claim-vs-evidence/three-things).

writerNotes: Disclosure required: Claude Opus 5.5 is named in the research (evaluated in RealCompanion; most token-hungry system, 546M vs 18M tokens at about the same F1) and the model writing this digest. State it neutrally; say tokens, not dollars.
No geography or political framing anywhere, including the company's home region and paper affiliations.
SCM: the 'every frame' tagline contradicts the README (frame sampling); attribute the tagline to the project and report what the README says.
RealCompanion is a preprint, not yet peer-reviewed; say 'about 0.7' F1, not 0.71.
Only 2 non-demo prior issues exist, so the 6-issue combination check covered both.
